candidate.statement: Prostate cancer cell lines with RB1 loss demonstrate greater dependency on E2F3 transcription factor activity.
queries: RB1 loss E2F3 dependency prostate cancer CRISPR
RB1 loss E2F3 CRISPR screen prostate

review.rationale: MED:41860961 provides direct empirical evidence showing synthetic lethality and selective dependency on E2F3 upon RB1 loss in prostate cancer models. Specifically, genome-wide CRISPR screens in transformed small cell neuroendocrine prostate cancer (SCPC) cell lines identified E2F3 dependency. Furthermore, isogenic PC3 prostate cancer cells with CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of RB1 exhibited marked proliferative arrest and impaired in vivo tumor growth upon E2F3 shRNA knockdown, whereas RB1 wild-type parental PC3 cells were unaffected, confirming greater dependency in the RB1-deficient state.

review.rationale: MED:41860961 specifically notes that across cancer cell lines in the DepMap dataset, phenotypic markers of RB inactivation include CDK4 dependency (as RB is the canonical target and its loss renders cells independent of CDK4/6; restoring RB restores CDK4/6i sensitivity). candidate.statement: Prostate cancer cell lines with PTEN loss exhibit increased dependency on PIK3CB (p110beta) compared to PTEN-wildtype cells, reflecting the established requirement of PI3K catalytic subunit beta for downstream signaling and tumorigenesis specifically in PTEN-deficient prostate cancer.
queries: PTEN loss PIK3CB dependency prostate cancer
PTEN deficient p110beta PIK3CB prostate cancer growth
PIK3CB knockout PTEN prostate cancer essentiality
PTEN PIK3CB DepMap prostate cell lines

review.rationale: The candidate asserts that prostate cancer cell lines with PTEN loss exhibit increased dependency on PIK3CB (p110beta) compared to PTEN-wildtype cells (direction -1 in DepMap dependency score, indicating stronger essentiality/dependency). Multiple sources provide direct empirical evidence: MED:18594509 demonstrates in an animal model of prostate tumor formation induced by Pten loss that ablation of Pik3cb (p110beta), but not Pik3ca (p110alpha), impeded tumorigenesis. MED:18755892 demonstrates that PTEN-deficient cancers specifically depend on PIK3CB knockdown (using inducible shRNA) for pathway activation and growth in vitro and in vivo. Furthermore, MED:41237375 directly investigates PTEN loss and PIK3CB reliance in prostate cancer (e.g., PC3 cells) and shows dependency on PIK3CB phosphorylation and signaling in PTEN-deficient contexts.

candidate.statement: Prostate cancer cell lines with PTEN loss exhibit increased genetic dependency on AKT2 compared to PTEN-wildtype cells, consistent with isoform-specific PI3K/AKT signaling downstream of PTEN deficiency.
queries: PTEN loss AKT2 dependency prostate cancer
PTEN deficient AKT2 knockdown prostate cancer viability
PTEN intact AKT1 AKT2 isoform dependency prostate

review.rationale: MED:37875657 directly evaluated prostate cancer cells isogenic for PTEN status and showed that PTEN deficiency correlated with specific dependence on AKT2 (alongside p110beta) for in vitro and in vivo parameters of metastatic growth and motility, whereas PTEN-expressing (wild-type) cells exhibited dependence on AKT1 and p110alpha instead. This primary empirical evidence directly supports the hypothesis that PTEN loss in prostate cancer leads to increased dependency on AKT2 compared to PTEN-intact/wild-type cells.

review.rationale: The proposed candidate is classified as neutral, evaluating whether CDKN2A loss associates with differential CDK4 dependency in prostate cancer cells within a specific subgroup defined by research signatures. None of the retrieved literature establishes an empirical directional association between CDKN2A status and CDK4 dependency specifically in prostate cancer or within the specified research signature subgroup. Because there is no established prior expectation contradicting neutrality for this specific lineage and subgroup combination, neutral is appropriate.
